mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility has accelerated monotonically from +6.7% to +21.0% over four weeks, indicating sustained lockdown compliance. This confinement suppresses retail-and-recreation mobility through reduced opportunity for non-essential outings. RETAIL_REC will remain depressed or decline further over the next four weeks as residential constraint persists.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the mean of the prior 28 days, or RESIDENTIAL mobility declines below +15% in any of the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility collapsed from +4.6% to -4.4% week-on-week (t-1w to t-0w), signaling a shift from essential shopping to panic-driven or deferred purchasing. This behavioral shock cascades to retail-and-recreation as consumers consolidate trips and reduce discretionary visits. RETAIL_REC will decline further as purchasing patterns remain disrupted.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below zero in current week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM dropped to -4.4% at t-0w from +4.6% at t-1w
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM returns to positive territory (>0%) within the next two weeks and RETAIL_REC does not decline further.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has declined monotonically from -20.6% to -55.4% over four weeks, indicating near-total collapse of public transport usage. This transport barrier directly constrains retail-and-recreation access for transit-dependent populations. RETAIL_REC will remain severely depressed over the next four weeks unless transit mobility recovers.
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility recovers to above -40% in any of the next two weeks and RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises above -40%.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has fallen from -16.0% to -40.6% over four weeks, reflecting escalating workplace closures and remote-work mandates. This employment shock reduces disposable income and eliminates weekday commute-adjacent retail opportunities. RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed over the next four weeks conditional on WORKPLACES staying below -35%.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility recovers above -30% within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC rises above -35% while WORKPLACES remains below -35%.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has collapsed from +27.3% to -15.6% over four weeks, indicating outdoor recreation has become constrained or discouraged. This shift reflects tightening behavioral restrictions on non-essential activities. The joint suppression of PARKS and RETAIL_REC signals a coordinated policy-driven reduction in discretionary mobility that will persist over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: PARKS mobility recovers above 0% within two weeks while RETAIL_REC remains below -40%, indicating decoupling of outdoor and retail constraints.

mechanism_narrative: The joint decline of TRANSIT (-55.4%) and WORKPLACES (-40.6%) at t-0w creates a compounding mobility deficit: reduced commuting eliminates both transport infrastructure usage and weekday retail foot traffic. This dual constraint will suppress RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks unless both series recover simultaneously.

failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES recovers above -30% within one week, and RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises above -40%.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -45% in the next week while RESIDENTIAL remains above +15% and GROCERY_PHARM remains below 0%.
